questions.title: A nurse is caring for a client hospitalized for the first time, which of the following actions ensure the safety of the client?

choices.title: Irrigate the tube with 30 mL of sterile water every hour, if needed
Reposition the tube if it is not draining well
Monitor the client for nausea, vomiting and abdominal distention
choices.correct_explanation:
• After a subtotal gastrectomy, a NG tube is commonly placed to prevent gastric distension and to facilitate drainage of stomach contents, which helps in reducing the risk of complications.   
  • The nurse should monitor the client for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distention because these symptoms may indicate that the NG tube is not functioning effectively (e.g., it may be blocked or displaced).   
  • Any of these signs could signal poor gastric drainage, which needs to be addressed to prevent further complications such as aspiration or gastric dilation.   
  • Therefore, option c: Monitor the client for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distention is correct.  

Incorrect answer:     

  • Irrigate the tube with 30 mL of sterile water every hour, if needed:  
    • Irrigating the NG tube should be avoided after a subtotal gastrectomy because it can increase tension on the suture line, which may impair healing.
    • The NG tube should be maintained at intermittent suction pressure to facilitate proper gastric decompression without causing harm.
  • Reposition the tube if it is not draining well:   
    • Repositioning the NG tube is not recommended unless specifically ordered by a healthcare provider.    
    • If drainage is sluggish, the nurse should assess for obstructions or dislodgement rather than manually repositioning the tube.
  • Turn the machine to high suction, if the drainage is sluggish on low suction:
    • High suction should be avoided as it can create excessive tension on the gastric suture line, potentially leading to complications.
    • Suction should always be kept at an intermittent level to prevent damage and promote proper healing.

choices.title: Turn the machine to high suction, if the drainage is sluggish on low suction

questions.title: A patient suffering from pain, was started on pain relieving therapy. During the therapy, nurse observes miosis and decreased respiratory rate. The patient also shows signs of sedation. What medication could be possibly causing these effects?

choices.title: Propranolol
choices.correct_explanation:
• The drug causing this case would be propranolol as this is a non-selective beta-blocker that blocks both beta 1 and 2 adrenergic receptors. Blocking beta 2 receptors in the lungs can cause bronchoconstriction, which can exacerbate or trigger asthma symptoms. Hence, option a. is correct.
  • Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker that affects the heart and blood vessels by reducing calcium influx. It is not known to cause bronchoconstriction or worsen asthma.
  • Nifedipine is also a calcium channel blocker, which works on the vascular smooth muscle to lower BP.
  • Captopril is an ACE inhibitor that causes a dry cough but does not cause asthma.

questions.title: <b>A patient is on medication for treatment of hypertension, during the therapy the drug is causing bronchoconstriction and asthma. What would be the probable drug?

choices.title: Epinephrine
choices.correct_explanation:
• Epinephrine augments hepatic glucose production by stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Although its effect on glycogenolysis rapidly wanes, hyperglycaemia continues because the effects of epinephrine on gluconeogenesis and glucose disposal persist.
  • Nor-epinephrine affects vasoconstriction and is less potent in stimulating glycogen breakdown and insulin release in comparison to epinephrine.
  • Dopamine does not stimulate glycogenolysis or insulin release.
  • Propranolol inhibits the effects of epinephrine and norepinephrine and thus will not stimulate insulin release or glycogenolysis.

questions.title: <b>Which medication causes glycogenolysis and insulin release?

  • Hypotension can occur with MgSO4 toxicity but is not the most critical effect in comparison to respiratory depression.

questions.title: What is the effect of MgSO4 toxicity?

choices.title: Vasoconstrictors
choices.correct_explanation:
• Dilated cardiomyopathy is a disease of the heart muscles characterized by enlargement and dilation of one or both of the ventricles along with impaired contractility. The drugs used for the management of dilated cardiomyopathy are:
    • Positive inotropes: It involves Digoxin to strengthen the heart muscle contractions.
    • Diuretics: These are used to reduce sodium and fluid retention from the body.
    • Vasodilators: It involves beta blockers and ACE inhibitors to lower blood pressure, improve blood flow and reduce the strain on the heart. Hence, options a, b and c are incorrect.
    • Vasoconstrictors: The use of these agents can increase impedance to ventricular ejection and impairs the performance of the dilated myopathic heart. Therefore, these drugs are contraindicated in dilated cardiomyopathy. Hence, option d is correct.

choices.title: Vulvar hematoma
choices.correct_explanation:
• Afterbirth pain is a common complaint in the postpartum client, but they are located in the uterus.
  • Constipation may cause rectal pressure but is not usually associated with severe pain.
  • Cystitis may cause pain, but the location is different.

  • When a postpartum patient complains of rectal pressure and severe pain in the perineum and if the symptoms are associated with swelling and discoloration of the vulva, a vulvar hematoma is a likely probability. A vulvar hematoma is a collection of blood in the soft tissues of the vulva, usually occurring due to trauma or a tear during childbirth. The blood accumulates in the tissue causing pressure, pain and swelling.
  • It is crucial for the nurse to recognize the signs and symptoms of a vulvar hematoma promptly. Timely assessment and intervention, often involving surgical drainage, are necessary to prevent complications and relieve the patient’s pain and discomfort.

questions.title: <b>During the first postpartum day, uterus is just lateral to the umbilicus indicating:

choices.title: Stop Oxytocin
choices.correct_explanation:
• The standard of care for an induction according to the Association of Women’s Health, Obstetric and Neonatal Nurses and American College of Obstetrics and Gynaecology is that contractions should not exceed 60 seconds in an induction. Inductions should simulate normal labor; 70-second contractions during the latent phase (3 cm) are not the norm. The next contractions can be longer and increase risks to the mother and fetus.
  • Contractions lasting 60-90 seconds during transition are typical; this provides a good distractor. The nurse needs to be knowledgeable of the phases and stages of labor.
  • So, the step should be to stop the oxytocin infusion. After that, FHT should be monitored continuously with an induction of labor; this is an accepted standard of care.

questions.title: A patient with 41-weeks of gestation is in labour unit with 3 cm cervix dilation, duration of contraction is 70 sec. Patient is on Oxytocin infusion. The nursing priority for this patient is to:

choices.title: The fetal head is at the level of the ischial spine
The fetal head is one centimeter below the ischial spine
The fetal head has not yet entered the pelvic inlet
choices.correct_explanation:
In obstetrics, station is a way of measuring the position of the fetal head in relation to the ischial spines of the pelvis:

  • Station 0 indicates that the fetal head is at the level of the ischial spines. When a fetal head is at the pelvic inlet, it is considered to be at "0 station"
  • Negative numbers (e.g., -1, -2) indicate that the fetal head is still above the ischial spines and has not yet entered the pelvic inlet.
  • Positive numbers (e.g., +1, +2) indicate that the fetal head has descended below the ischial spines toward the pelvic outlet.

When the fetal head is at -1 station, it means the fetal head is 1 centimeter above the ischial spines, and it has not yet entered the pelvic inlet.

So, the correct interpretation is that the fetal head has not yet entered the pelvic inlet.

choices.title: The fetal head is located in the pelvic outlet

questions.title: A nurse is conducting a vaginal examination on a pregnant client in labor. The nurse assesses that the fetal head is at a station of -1. What does this station value indicate regarding the fetal head’s position in the pelvis?

choices.title: Two centimetre below the ischial spine
choices.correct_explanation:
• Fetal station in obstetrics refers to the position of the presenting part of the baby in relation to the ischial spine of the mother’s pelvis.
  • A station of +2 means that the baby’s head is descended two centimeter below the ischial spine but has not yet entered the birth canal (vaginal canal). This indicates that the baby’s head is engaged in the pelvis and is descending further down in preparation for delivery.

  • When a fetal head is at the pelvic outlet, it is considered to be at a " +5 station"

choices.title: One centimetre above the ischial spine
Has not entered the pelvic inlet yet

choices.title: Immediately, pour sterile saline on the cord and repeat every 15 minutes to prevent drying
Cover the cord with a wet sponge
Apply a cord clamp to the exposed cord and cover with a sterile towel
Keep the cord warm and moist by continuous applications of warm sterile saline compresses
choices.correct_explanation:
• The immediate priority is to minimize pressure on the cord. Thus, the nurse’s initial action involves placing the client on bed rest and then placing the client in a knee-chest position or lowering the head of the bed and elevating the maternal hips on a pillow to minimize the pressure on the cord (Trendelenburg Position). In the given case, if umbilical cord is prolapsing, or visible outside the vagina, it is crucial for the nurse to keep the cord warm and moist to prevent it from drying. Use of warm sterile saline maintains the cord’s moisture and temperature. Hence, option d. is correct.
  • Option a: Saline should be warmed; waiting 15 minutes may not keep the cord moist.
  • Option b: This choice does not specify what the sponge was wet with, information is inadequate.
  • Option c: This measure would stop circulation to the fetus.
  • Option d: The cord should be kept warm and moist to maintain fetal circulation. This measure is an accepted nursing action.

questions.title: In addition to changing the mother’s position to relieve cord pressure, the nurse may employ the following measures in the event when she observes that the cord is out of the vagina:

choices.title: A non-reactive test
choices.correct_explanation:
A reactive non-stress test (NST) requires at least two fetal heart rate accelerations of ≥15 beats/min above the baseline, each lasting ≥15 seconds, within a 20-minute period (for fetuses ≥32 weeks gestation).

In this question, although accelerations occurred three times and lasted 15 seconds, the increase in fetal heart rate was only 5 beats/min, which does not meet the amplitude criterion for a reactive NST.

Therefore, the NST is interpreted as non-reactive.

  • Reactive test: ≥15 bpm acceleration lasting ≥15 seconds (2 times in 20 min)
  • Non-reactive test: Criteria for reactivity not met
  • Unsatisfactory test: Usually due to technical issues or inability to obtain an interpretable tracing
  • Negative test: Term used for contraction stress tests, not NST

questions.title: After the fetal activity test (non-stress test) is completed, the nurse is looking at the test results on the monitor strip. choices.correct_explanation:

choices.title: SSI (Surgical Site Infection)
choices.correct_explanation:
• Surgical site infections are the most common nosocomial infections to occur after a surgical procedure. The causative organisms are both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumonia, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter, and Proteus mirabilis. Hence, option b is correct.
  • The other nosocomial infections such as pneumonia, atelectasis and SIRS (Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome) are not the most common one.
  • Pneumonia is less common than SSIs as a nosocomial infection post-surgery.
  • SIRS is a systemic inflammatory response but may not be a specific infection itself.
  • Atelectasis is a common post-operative complication but it is not classified as an infection.

questions.title: <b>Which of the following nosocomial infection is most common to occur after a surgery?

choices.title: Post-transfusion related acute lung injury (TRALI)
choices.correct_explanation:
• TRALI is a serious and potentially life-threatening reaction that typically occurs within 6 hours of a blood transfusion. It is characterized by tachycardia, difficulty breathing (dyspnea), and hypoxemia, often leading to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). TRALI is thought to be caused by the recipient's immune response to white blood cells in the transfused blood, triggering inflammation in the lungs.

Here’s why the other options are less likely:

  • Allergic reaction (option a) can cause symptoms like hives, itching, and anaphylaxis, but it usually doesn't cause the respiratory distress and tachycardia seen in TRALI.
  • Acute hemolytic reaction (option b) typically presents with fever, chills, back pain, dark urine, and shock due to a mismatch in blood type, but it usually doesn't cause significant respiratory distress.
  • Septic reaction (option d) would result from contamination of the blood product, leading to fever, chills, hypotension, and signs of infection, but it doesn’t typically present with respiratory distress as the primary symptom.

TRALI is the most likely cause of the symptoms in this scenario.

  • Anaphylactic reaction is a severe, life-threatening reaction characterized by bronchospasm, hypotension, and difficulty breathing.

questions.title: A pacemaker is placed on a patient and discharged after 8 days. What is the least priority teaching to be given by the nurse?

choices.title: Administering oxygen via nasal cannula at 2 liters per minute
Placing the patient in a high Fowler’s position
Initiating Non-Invasive Positive Pressure Ventilation (NIPPV)
choices.correct_explanation:
• Unconscious patients with signs of respiratory distress require immediate intervention to maintain adequate oxygenation. NIPPV, such as BiPAP (Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure) or CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure), is a priority intervention.
  • NIPPV helps improve oxygenation and ventilation by delivering positive pressure during inhalation and exhalation, reducing the work of breathing and supporting oxygen exchange in the lungs. It is especially beneficial in patients with respiratory distress, as it can prevent the need for invasive mechanical ventilation.
  • Options a and b are not the most appropriate interventions for a patient in severe respiratory distress. Administering low-flow oxygen via nasal cannula may not provide sufficient support and placing the patient in a high Fowler’s position alone might not be enough to alleviate the distress.
  • Administering an analgesic (option d) can be considered if pain is contributing to the distress, but addressing the immediate respiratory issue is the priority to ensure adequate oxygenation. NIPPV, when initiated promptly can significantly improve the patient’s respiratory status and prevent further deterioration.

questions.title: <b>A patient is presented with symptoms of confusion, seizures, tremors etc. Which electrolyte imbalance can be suspected in this patient?

choices.title: Metabolic acidosis
choices.correct_explanation:
• The client with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) most often has metabolic acidosis which can also cause hyperkalemia. In DKA, the breakdown of fats for energy produces ketone bodies, acidic in nature. This results in low ph, decreased serum bicarbonate, and anion gap metabolism acidosis.
  • Metabolic acidosis is present with Kussmaul breathing.

  • Hypokalemia results from shift of potassium back into cells and is not associated with DKA.
  • Hypernatremia occurs in the case of severe dehydration.
  • DKA is associated with hyperglycemia rather than hypoglycemia.

questions.title: Which electrolyte imbalance can be seen in a patient with diabetic ketoacidosis?

choices.title: Brain
choices.correct_explanation:
• Drowning can cause an irreversible brain injury or damage in the hippocampus, basal ganglia and cerebral cortex due to interrupted oxygen supply. Hence, option c is correct.
  • Lungs are critically affected due to drowning, leading to fluid accumulation but is usually not irreversible, if treated promptly and effectively.
  • Kidneys can also be affected due to drowning, if there is severe dehydration or electrolyte imbalances. However, the most critical damage occurs to the brain rather than kidneys.
  • Heart also suffers from drowning but the irreversible damage is caused to the brain due to prolonged hypoxia.

questions.title: <b>Which organ has the highest risk of irreversible damage due to drowning?

choices.title: Shift the client to nasal cannula
Obtain the sample without any change
choices.correct_explanation:
• As per the given scenario, the client is receiving oxygen through non-rebreather mask. The Non-Rebreather Mask (NRM) is indicated in case of client who requires high concentration of oxygen; this itself signifies that we can’t obtain the sample by removing the client from the NRM.
  • Option a and b: Subject to doctor’s order.
  • Option d: We can keep the client at room air for 20-30 minutes before sampling but only if the client is stable and with patent airway. Always remember oxygen is the most basic physiological need as per the Maslow’s hierarchy of human needs.

choices.title: Keep the client on room air for 30 minutes

choices.title: Heimlich maneuver
choices.correct_explanation:
• The episodes of labored breathing and shortness of breath are due to the presence of foreign body in the respiratory tract. Therefore, the nurse should immediately perform Heimlich maneuver or abdominal thrust in conscious victim to expel out the foreign body. Hence, option b is correct.

Figure: Heimlich maneuver

  • Gower’s maneuver is associated with Duchene muscular dystrophy.

Figure: Gower’s maneuver

  • Crede’s maneuver is used to separate placenta after delivery or to void urine by manual pressure in case of urinary retention.

Figure: Crede’s maneuver

  • Merely providing oxygen support will not relieve labored breathing as the cause is foreign body obstruction.

choices.title: “I should take Aspirin with a full glass of water.”
“It’s best to take Aspirin on an empty stomach for faster absorption.”
choices.correct_explanation:
• Aspirin, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), is commonly used to relieve pain, reduce inflammation and lower fever.
  • To maximize its effectiveness and minimize the risk of stomach irritation, it should be taken with food or after eating.
  • Taking Aspirin with a full glass of water or with milk helps to prevent stomach upset.
  • Crushing or chewing Aspirin tablets can increase the risk of irritation and should be avoided. It is essential for patients to take Aspirin as prescribed by their healthcare provider and follow the recommended instructions to ensure safe and effective use.

choices.title: “I should avoid crushing or chewing the Aspirin tablet.”
“I can take Aspirin with milk to reduce stomach irritation.”

choices.title: Hematoma formation and compressing the site
choices.correct_explanation:
•     If a vein is pricked instead of an artery during collection of ABG sample, there is a chance of formation of hematoma. It may occur due to high pressure flow difference. Therefore, the nurse should compress the site by applying pressure to stop the bleeding and prevent a hematoma from worsening. Hence, option a. is correct.  

•     The nurse should not send the sample to lab as blood from a vein is not suitable for ABG analysis. Hence, option b. is incorrect.

•     The nurse can take sample from another hand, however, the priority is to manage the puncture site to prevent or control hematoma formation. Hence, option c. is incorrect.

•     Maintaining records is essential, however, this can be done once the patient is stabilized. Hence, option d. is incorrect.

choices.title: Blood clot, send it to the lab

choices.title: Onion, garlic, egg, cabbage
choices.correct_explanation:
• The food items to be avoided to prevent odor in colostomy patients are onion, egg, garlic, cabbage, fish, asparagus, broccoli, etc. Hence, option a is correct.
  • Liquid, clear water, and juice do not cause foul odor in stool, instead they are suggested for patients with colostomy to maintain fluid balance and ensure output is easier to manage.
  • Beer, nuts, and popcorn can cause gas and odor but popcorn and nuts don’t contribute to foul odor of stool.
  • Bottle gourd and sweet potato do not produce foul-smelling gas.

choices.title: Hypomagnesemia
choices.correct_explanation:
• Hypomagnesemia can occur in patients with chronic alcohol use through reduced intestinal absorption, increased urinary losses and intracellular shift of magnesium. Hence, option c is correct.
  • Hyperkalemia is less common in chronic alcoholism unless there is an underlying renal failure. Moreover, the patient of the given case has dehydration, which causes hypokalemia rather than hyperkalemia.
  • Hypercalcemia is related to hyperparathyroidism, excessive vitamin D intake, etc. Alcoholism is not a common cause for hypercalcemia.
  • Hyperphosphatemia is associated with renal failure, excessive phosphorus intake, rhabdomyolysis, etc. In the alcoholic patients, hypophosphatemia is seen rather than hyperphosphatemia due to poor nutrition.

questions.title: <b>A 40-year-old male, Sam with a history of alcoholism, is admitted for severe dehydration. What electrolyte imbalance is he most at risk for?

choices.title: Airway flow
choices.correct_explanation:
• When the patient is shifted to PACU, the nurse should assess the respiratory status first, then breathing and circulation. In respiratory assessment, airway patency and flow should be initially assessed. Oxygen saturation, breath sounds and RR are assessed afterwards. Hence, option d is correct.
  • Oxygen saturation should be assessed once the nurse has confirmed that the airway is clear and patient is breathing effectively.
  • Respiratory rate should be assessed after ensuring that the airway is patent and airflow is adequate.
  • Breath sounds provide information about the lungs’ condition and they should be assessed after confirming that the airway is clear.

choices.title: Hypokalemia
choices.correct_explanation:
• The dehydration is caused due to excessive sweating and low potassium levels leads to muscle spasm and weakness. The athlete in this case must be suffering with hypokalemia. Hence, option a is correct.
  • Hyperkalemia is characterized by muscle weakness, fatigue, and cardiac arrhythmias.
  • Hypocalcemia is characterized by muscle cramps and spasms but it doesn’t cause profuse sweating or dizziness.
  • Hypercalcemia is characterized by fatigue, confusion, and nausea but does not cause profuse sweating or dizziness.

choices.correct_explanation:
• The key indicators for assessment of fluid adequacy are:

  • SpO2 measures the oxygen level in the blood and is relevant for respiratory status rather than the fluid balance.

choices.title: Giving Tetracycline to a child younger than 8 years may cause permanent staining of his teeth
choices.correct_explanation:
• Tetracycline is avoided during tooth development as it interferes with enamel formation and dental pigmentation. Hence, option a is correct.
  • Tetracycline should not be given with milk as the milk interferes with the absorption of the drug. Hence, option b is incorrect.
  • Tetracycline is avoided in children under the age of tooth development. However, it is not avoided in children of all age groups. Hence, option c is incorrect.
  • Secondary infections of chronic skin disorders respond to antibiotics such as Tetracycline. Hence, option d is also incorrect.

choices.correct_explanation:
• Ribavirin inhibits replication of the respiratory syncytial virus. It is an antiviral agent available in crystal form which is reconstituted with sterile water. It is administered via aerosolization to decrease the duration of viral shedding within the infected tissue. Hence, option d is correct.
  • It is not administered via oral or IM route. Hence, option a and b are incorrect.
  • Ribavirin is not approved for IV use to treat RSV in children. Hence, option c is incorrect.

choices.title: Fluid volume deficit
choices.correct_explanation:
·         The emergent phase lasts for 48 to 72 hours from the time the burn occurs. There is excessive urination leading to fluid volume deficit in the patient. Thus, the nurse should look for diuresis as a potential complication in this phase of injury. Hence, option a is correct.

·         The other options do not occur after 48 hours of burn injury.

·         Option (b): Fluid volume excess: This is more likely before diuresis begins or due to over-resuscitation. After 48 hours, diuresis leads to fluid loss, not excess.

·         Option (c): Decreased cardiac output: Typically, a concern during the initial shock phase (first 24–48 hours) due to fluid shifts, not after 48 hours.

·         Option (d): Severe hypotension: Also more common during the initial emergent phase, especially if fluid replacement is inadequate.

Answering a Question

  1. Each question will have four options, out of which only one must be selected.
  2. You will receive 1 mark for every correct answer, and 0.33 mark (1/3rd) will be deducted for each incorrect answer.
  3. Click the option you want to mark, in case you want to another question simply select another option the first selection will be automatically omitted.
  4. To attempt the next question click on next to attempt the previous Question click on previous
  5. You can bookmark the Question or also report a question
